clue.text: Duke has finished the port

parts.note: something finished is over

explanation.surface: A duke has completed his business at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is the Kent harbour town facing France, England's busiest ferry port.

clue.text: Getting low grades in test can be a distressing experience

explanation.surface: Failing marks in an exam can be upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening words are padding for the surface; the two definitions are 'test' (trial by ordeal) and 'distressing experience'.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval trial by ordeal was a test of guilt, and the word now means any painful, harrowing experience.

clue.text: Farm worker showing elegance ahead of the woman with diamonds!

parts.note: neat suggests tidy elegance, as in a neat outfit
her stands for the woman
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A stylish labourer walks in front of a lady wearing diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elegance' is a noun but stands for the adjective NEAT; the looseness is common in charades.
explanation.definitionFit: A neatherd is an old word for a cowherd, someone who tends cattle on a farm.

clue.text: Allure of a Thailand region

parts.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
a tract is a stretch or region of land

explanation.surface: The appeal of an area of Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: To allure is to draw or tempt someone, a verb sense shared with the answer.

clue.text: Sandy finishing in this athletics event

definitions.text: Sandy finishing in this athletics event

parts.words: Sandy finishing in this athletics event
parts.note: read as a field event whose competitors end up landing in a sand pit, not a person called Sandy

explanation.surface: Someone named Sandy comes last in this sports contest.
explanation.definitionFit: In this field event the athlete sprints and leaps, landing in a pit of sand.

clue.text: About to enter fortification to obtain submission

indicators.note: to enter means the short word for about goes inside the fortification word

parts.note: a defence is a fortification
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Getting inside a fort to force surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: Deference is respectful yielding to another, a form of submission.

clue.text: To get cure, cooked a vegetable

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of to get cure are prepared afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Eating a cooked vegetable as a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The courgette, or zucchini, is a small marrow eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Individual getting rid of last son has a big problem

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Individual getting rid of last son has a big problem (5)' for POSER; 'big problem' defines it but no word for 'individual' loses a son or S to leave POSE, and a search found nothing, so the clue looks garbled.
annotationWithheld.clue: Individual getting rid of last son has a big problem

clue.text: Blockhead putting off quiet friend

indicators.note: putting off means the letter for quiet is dropped from the end of the dunce word

parts.note: a chump is a blockhead, a fool
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A dimwit tells a mate to keep his voice down.
explanation.definitionFit: A chum is a close pal or companion.

clue.text: Gun agent joins someone having a meal

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
an eater is someone having a meal

explanation.surface: A gunman agent sits down with a diner.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is a firearm that fires several shots without reloading.

clue.text: He hugs erratic, reclusive American multi-millionaire

indicators.note: erratic suggests the letters of he hugs are behaving unpredictably and rearranged

explanation.surface: A wealthy American recluse hugs someone unpredictably.
explanation.walkthrough: Howard Hughes was the American aviator and film producer who became famously reclusive.
explanation.definitionFit: Howard Hughes was a billionaire tycoon who spent his last years in seclusion.

clue.text: Get away from sound of insect

indicators.note: sound of tells us the insect word is heard, not written

parts.note: a flea is a jumping insect

explanation.surface: Running from the buzzing of a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away from danger, escape.

clue.text: Man on train perhaps needing power for minute palmtop?

indicators.note: needing power for minute means one letter is swapped for another in the traveller word
needing power for minute means one letter is swapped for another in the traveller word

parts.note: a commuter is someone who travels by train to work
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A rail traveller needs electricity for a tiny handheld gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like tiny, describing the palmtop, but it is M; the question mark flags the palmtop as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmtop is a small handheld example of a computing machine.

clue.text: Little right in maths — I go wrong making chart

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for right is placed inside the rearranged letters
wrong signals that maths, I and go are put into a different order

parts.note: R is the short, little, form of right

explanation.surface: Messing up my maths while drawing a graph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' looks like part of the instruction 'go wrong', but it is fodder; only 'wrong' signals the shuffle, giving HISTOGAM before 'in' adds the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A histogram is a bar diagram showing frequency distribution, a type of statistical graph.

clue.text: Rough water when one gets to port during journey

indicators.note: during means the one-plus-port piece occurs within the journey word

parts.note: a ride is a journey
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Choppy seas when a traveller reaches harbour mid-voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as a definition or a harbour town, but here it is just its abbreviation, joined to the one by 'gets to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A riptide is a strong turbulent current, choppy and dangerous water.

clue.text: Assistant turning up to follow those people in TV, newspapers, etc

indicators.note: to follow means the assistant piece comes after the word for those people

parts.note: them refers to those people

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the assistant word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: A helper looks on at people working in broadcasting and the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses AIDE to EDIA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectively, broadcasting and the press are known as the mass communication industry.

clue.text: Sharp tool I choose to break into church? On the contrary!

indicators.note: to break into suggests one piece entering another, here the church goes inside
On the contrary reverses the stated direction so church takes the inside role

parts.note: to pick is to choose
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A burglar's sharp instrument chosen for raiding a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'I choose' would break into church; 'On the contrary' flips the roles, so church goes inside instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice pick is a pointed implement for chipping ice, a sharp tool.

clue.text: Boy embracing Ivan excitedly in celebration

indicators.note: embracing means the boy's name wraps around the other letters

parts.note: Carl is a boy's name

indicators.note: excitedly suggests the letters of Ivan are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A lad hugs Ivan in high spirits at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' rearranges Ivan's letters into NIVA, and 'embracing' puts them inside the boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a festive public celebration with parades and revelry.

clue.text: Blessing from mountain peak is feasible

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish word for a mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis
taken as written
something feasible is on, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: Divine favour comes from the summit if possible.
explanation.definitionFit: A benison is an old literary word for a benediction or blessing.

clue.text: Cheap accommodation always taken in portion of journey

indicators.note: taken in means the always word is housed inside the journey-section word

parts.note: a stage is a portion of a journey
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Budget lodging is always included on one leg of a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest class of passenger berth on a ship.

clue.text: Dancing girl in paradisial mansion

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the phrase paradisial mansion

explanation.surface: A dancer performs in a heavenly mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: An alma, or almah, is an Egyptian professional female dancer and singer.

clue.text: Bird in castle

explanation.surface: A bird nests in a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A crow-like bird shares its name with the chess piece also called the castle.

clue.text: Drug I took at meal perhaps after operation

indicators.note: after means the I and the eating word come behind the operation abbreviation

parts.note: ate means took food, as one does at a meal

explanation.surface: Medication I took with food following surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a narcotic derived from opium, such as morphine.

clue.text: Politician appearing after special news item

indicators.note: appearing after means the politician comes behind the special abbreviation

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A Conservative MP shows up after a special news report.
explanation.definitionFit: A news story is a single report or article in the press.

clue.text: Shining silver at special meal

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: special suggests the letters of meal are treated in an unusual way, rearranged

explanation.surface: Silverware glitters at a special dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' looks like an adjective for the meal, but it rearranges the letters of meal into LEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Agleam means gleaming or glowing with light.

clue.text: Found a tent with three upright members buckling

indicators.note: buckling suggests the tent collapses, its letters bent into a new shape

parts.note: III, three vertical strokes, is the Roman numeral three

explanation.surface: A tent with three upright poles is collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buckling' rearranges A, TENT and III; 'Found' is the verb to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found something is to start or establish it, as one might begin a society.

clue.text: A supply of wine taken to cold compartment

indicators.note: taken to means the A and the wine store come after the letter for cold

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
a bin is a rack or stock of wine

explanation.surface: Some wine is carried to the chilled section.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is an enclosed room on a ship or aircraft, a compartment.

clue.text: Religious group in control, holding on

indicators.note: holding means the control word grips the short word inside it

parts.note: mastery means control

explanation.surface: A faith community stays in charge and hangs on.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery houses a community of monks, a body of religious people.
